anomalies.observed: On the AVR-ISP-6 programming header J5 the SCK and /RESET signals are placed on the wrong physical pins: pin 3 carries the RST label and the net NET0003 (the MCU reset line, also pulled up by R6 and tied to U1/U2 pin 1 /PB5), while pin 5 carries the SCK label and the net NET0001 (the MCU SCK line, tied to U1/U2 pin 7 /PB2). The remaining pins (1=MISO/NET0011, 4=MOSI/NET0007, 2=VCC, 6=GND) are correct.
anomalies.expected: The standard 2x3 AVR-ISP-6 connector pinout is pin 3 = SCK and pin 5 = /RESET. The SCK net (NET0001) should be on pin 3 and the reset net (NET0003) on pin 5 so that a standard ISP programmer/cable matches the board.

evidence.quote: Sheet / (fan_controller.kicad_sch): J5 'AVR-ISP-6' shows pin 3 labelled RST -> NET0003 and pin 5 labelled SCK -> NET0001
U1/U2 pin 1 (RESET/PB5) -> NET0003; U1/U2 pin 7 (PB2) -> NET0001; R6 10K between +5V and NET0003 (reset pull-up)
spec describes fan_controller only as 'an ATtiny-driven fan controller' (Atmel/), leaving the ISP header pinout to standard practice

anomalies.impact: The SCK and RESET lines are swapped on the programming header. A standard AVR ISP programmer would drive the MCU reset line with the clock and tie the reset line to the programmer's reset pin, so the device cannot be programmed (and the MCU may be held in reset or glitched) unless the cable is rewired.

parsed.summary: The board is a coherent ATtiny fan controller (SMD/THT MCU alternatives, 5 V regulator, pot input, I2C header, PMOS fan driver), but the AVR-ISP-6 header J5 has its SCK and /RESET nets swapped onto pins 5 and 3 instead of the standard 3 and 5, which would prevent programming with a normal ISP cable; this is the only deviation the drawing supports, and my confidence is moderate because the small pin labels are partly ambiguous.
